body:
@codex review

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=7fac90f3 round=1 -->

@codex review the previous round fixed a decision rule whose conditional terminal branches did not
cover their input space: a state matched only a "continue" branch, every terminating branch was
guarded by a condition that state failed, and the caller looped forever. List every occurrence of
that same shape you can find across this procedure's decision tables and guard conditions, in this
one comment, rather than the first one.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=54514caf round=2 -->

@codex review the previous round fixed a rule that this branch restated in one place while an
instruction elsewhere in the same procedure still told the reader to do the thing the restatement
forbade, so the two could not both be followed. List every occurrence of that same shape you can
find between this branch's rewritten rules and the steps, tables and notes that were not rewritten
with them, in this one comment, rather than the first one.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=9d469e5e round=3 -->

@codex review the previous rounds each found one state or identifier this branch introduced that was
classified, bounded or reported inconsistently. Sweep for the remaining members of that space: every
new abort reason, marker key, condition and state this branch adds — check each is produced by some
path, defined where it is used, and reported under the same name everywhere it appears, and name any
that is reachable but never described or described but never reachable. List them all in this one
comment rather than the first one.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=cfc9a6a8 round=4 -->

@codex review the previous round fixed a lookup that was correct until this branch changed a
precondition it silently depended on — a round could not previously reopen on an unchanged commit,
and once it could, a search keyed on the commit was wrong. Sweep for the rest of that space: for each
assumption this branch weakens or removes (a round fires one trigger; a round's triggers all differ
in commit; a verdict names one review; a trigger is always the newest comment), find every rule,
count, filter, reply or report elsewhere in the procedure that still relies on the old form. List
them all in this one comment rather than the first one.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=b9a54623 round=5 -->

@codex review the previous round fixed two promises this branch makes in one step that are
unreachable from the path that needs them — a recovery documented in step 10 but reached only from
one verdict, and a recovery documented in step 7 but invisible to the read that would trigger it.
Sweep for the rest of that class: for every guarantee, recovery or "this is recorded / reported /
recovered" claim this branch adds, trace whether some reachable path actually performs it, and name
each one that is stated but cannot run, or runs but is never stated. List them all in this one
comment rather than the first one.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=9d46c2bf round=6 -->

@codex review the previous round fixed a comparison that used a coarser key than the mechanism it was
reasoning about — a second-resolution timestamp standing in for the fence's (createdAt, databaseId)
ordering. Sweep for the rest of that class across this branch: every comparison, match or lookup it
adds that stands in for a finer-grained fact — timestamps against ids, prefixes against whole values,
a commit against a round, a name against an identity — and name each place the coarser key can differ
from the thing it is being used to decide. List them all in this one comment rather than the first
one.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=2967ca2c round=7 -->

@codex review the previous round fixed a rule that searched a structured payload as raw text instead
of parsing it into whole fields, so a longer value satisfied a search for a shorter one. Sweep for the
rest of that class across this branch: every place it reads a structured thing — a marker payload, a
fence output line, an API field, a reason string — and decides from a substring, a prefix or a
contains rather than from a parsed whole value, and name each one where a longer or quoted value can
satisfy the test. List them all in this one comment rather than the first one.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=1598a30f round=8 -->

@codex review the previous round fixed a rule that had been corrected in one place and left
standing in five others, which is the third time on this branch that a statement was edited instead of
the rule. Sweep the whole branch for that class one more time: for every rule, number, threshold,
bound and classification this branch introduces or changes, find every place it is stated across the
procedure, the two docs, the skill router and the changelog, and name each set where the statements no
longer agree. List them all in this one comment rather than the first one.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=b9a626cb round=9 -->

@codex review the previous round reconciled five sets of statements that had drifted apart, and
the class before it was the same. Sweep once more across the whole branch for any rule, number,
threshold, bound or classification that is stated in more than one place and no longer agrees, and
say explicitly if you find none. List everything in this one comment rather than the first one.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=1176df08 round=10 -->
@codex review

@codex review the previous round fixed a rule whose explanatory paragraph carried a required
distinction while the two statements that instruct — a prose rule and a decision-table row — still
stated it absolutely, so following the procedure gave a different answer than reading it. List every
occurrence of that same shape you can find, in this one comment, rather than the first one: any rule,
cost, bound, threshold or classification whose narrative explanation and whose normative statement
(a table row, a lettered condition, or an imperative sentence) do not agree.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=29678230 round=11 -->

@codex review the previous round closed the four sets you listed, so the normative copies now carry
the distinctions their explanatory paragraphs required. Two follow-on classes are worth the same
treatment, and I would rather have every occurrence of both in this one comment than the first of
either. First, the inverse of what you found: a claim that is now stale because the text it described
moved — an explanation, a changelog entry, a doc summary or a test comment that still describes an
older rule, count, threshold or list. Second, any remaining place where a rule's scope is asserted
more narrowly or more broadly than the rule itself — "only", "every", "always", "never", "the one",
"all of them" — and the qualification lives somewhere else or nowhere.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=1c7ed059 round=12 -->

@codex review the previous round closed five sets, and two of them were defects the round before had
introduced — a qualification added beside an absolute statement that was left standing. That is the
shape to hunt now, and I would rather have every occurrence in this one comment than the first.
Look for any rule this branch has edited where the new text was added next to the old rather than
replacing it, so a reader following the nearest sentence still gets the superseded answer: an
imperative still stating a rule its own paragraph now qualifies, a summary or count that predates a
list it introduces, a condition named in one place and enumerated differently in another, or a filter
stated in the operative rule and dropped in every restatement of it.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=89801d32 round=13 -->

@codex review the previous round's two sharpest findings were control flow rather than wording: an
ordered pre-check that aborted before a later rule could run, and a step that assumed a value an
earlier step no longer always emits. That is the class to hunt now, and I want every occurrence in
this one comment rather than the first. Trace the paths a reader actually walks and find where one
step assumes something another no longer guarantees: an ordered check that decides before a later
rule is consulted, a step that reads a field its predecessor emits only on some paths, a value
produced under one condition and consumed under a weaker one, a cross-reference to a step or a
section that no longer does what the reference says, and any instruction whose precondition is
stated only somewhere else.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=53e8a374 round=14 -->

@codex review the previous round was a P1: step 9's ordered pre-checks asked every verdict for fields
only some verdicts carry, so `pending` could satisfy neither (c) nor (d) and the whole re-post path
was unreachable. The fix names, per check, which signal forms it applies to. Sweep that same class
across the rest of the procedure and give me every occurrence in this one comment rather than the
first: any instruction that reads a value some producer does not always supply, any enumeration whose
cases do not cover what its producer can actually emit, and any place where the procedure's prose
disagrees with the fence text it is describing. Read the three fenced scripts as the authority on what
is produced, and say for each finding which fence line proves it.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=a26d4a84 round=15 -->

@codex review the last two rounds were both P1s of one class: the prose describing a fence disagreed
with the fence's own text. Four such mismatches were closed last round. Keep reading the three fenced
scripts as the authority and give me every remaining occurrence in this one comment rather than the
first, citing the fence line that proves each. Worth pressing on: the awk and jq field positions the
prose names, the comparison operators and their strictness, what each `exit 0` path actually prints
versus what the tables say it prints, the wait-ci and merge fences which have had far less attention
than wait-verdict, and any claim about `gh` behaviour at the documented 2.4.0 floor that the fences
would disprove.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=ea9f5272 round=16 -->

**Re: the round 16 review** (`5062480632`) — fixed in round 17 (`0e5fd09`).

This reply is a pull request comment rather than an inline one because **that review had no inline comments to reply to**, which is also the most important thing it found.

## The review the procedure would have called clean

`pulls/13/comments` returned **zero** rows for that review's `pull_request_review_id`, and the entire P1 — severity badge and five sub-findings — was in the review body. Step 10 opened with "**a review body is boilerplate or empty; the findings are inline review comments**", and step 9's table read a review with zero inline comments as a **clean finish**. Following either would have reported a P1 round as clean, and under `--auto --merge` merged past it.

I only caught it because I read the body before acting on the count. That is luck, not design, so the design is changed: step 10 now reads the body as well as the comments and treats a body carrying a severity badge as findings, the table row is "not clean by itself", and `reviewers/codex.md` records the observation — every earlier round on this pull request put its findings inline, so this is a **tendency, not a contract**, and one observation means the frequency is unknown rather than rare.

## The five findings

**`PENDING` on the direct path** — right, and it is mine. Last round I added the exclusion to step 10's two-trigger REST sweep only. The fence admits every review that is not `DISMISSED` and drops `state` from its output, so a draft reaches `VERDICT=review` indistinguishable from a submitted one, and with no inline comments lands on the clean row. Step 10's new body read doubles as the state check, so the single-trigger path is covered by the same call.

**Step 12's "falls back to `retry`"** — right. A fifth consecutive fetch failure is `CI_WAIT=error reason=api`; a completed non-success is `CHECKS_FAILED`. Only zero rows, a malformed row and a still-running row retry. The sentence now says which is which, and keeps the point the naive check breaks.

**Terminal exits and continue rows** — right, and a good catch on the reasoning rather than the wording. The fence exits for **every** review, so the ancestor row's "continue (once)" *is* a terminal exit. It is safe because the caller allows one re-fire and aborts on the second — bounded by the caller, not by the fence. `## Notes` now says that instead of forbidding what the fence actually does.

**"Every fence resolves the branch first"** — right. `wait-verdict` reads `gh repo view` first and can exit `api stage=setup` before the branch is looked at. What actually holds is that nothing reaches `gh pr list` without a non-empty branch, which is where the guard has to hold; that is what it says now.

**The merge response body** — right. Every abort exits before the PUT is fired, so `RESP` does not exist. `MERGE=failed` carries a body worth quoting; `MERGE=abort` has none and the reason is the whole signal.

## Not changed, deliberately

The fence's own `state` filter and the review selection's same-second tie-break remain **known gaps recorded in `## Notes`**, not fixed — both are fence edits, and a fence edit costs every user a re-approval. That is still not mine to spend unasked.

**No fence changed**: `tests/fence-hashes.txt` is untouched and all three fences report matching. Verified: `npm run check:all` exit 0 (fence-guards 28/28, wait-verdict 72, wait-ci 15, merge 16, jq-program 22, permissions 25, procedure-refs 38, provenance 24, schema 22, version 7) and `npm run audit` (0 vulnerabilities).

@codex review the previous round's review had zero inline comments and its whole P1 in the review
body, which two rules in this procedure said could not happen — so that round would have been read as
clean. Both are fixed. Keep the fences as the authority and give me every remaining occurrence in
this one comment rather than the first, citing what proves each. Two seams are worth pressing: places
where the procedure asserts the shape of data it did not produce — GitHub's API responses, the
reviewer's output, `gh`'s behaviour — and states it as a contract rather than as something measured;
and the enumerations that decide a terminal outcome, where a case nobody listed lands on a clean
finish or a merge rather than on a stop.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=0e5fd09e round=17 -->

@codex review the previous round's three P1s were all defects the round before it introduced, and all
three were the same shape: a rule applied to one of two readers, an enumeration with no default, and
a retry with no bound. The fix routes both readers through one state table whose default is a stop.
Give me every remaining occurrence of those three shapes in this one comment rather than the first,
citing what proves each. Concretely: any rule that two code paths are supposed to share where only
one carries it, any enumeration or table that decides a terminal outcome without a stop default, and
any retry, re-fire or loop whose bound is stated somewhere other than where the retry is written.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=b7ec1678 round=18 -->

@codex review the previous round collapsed the two review readers into one named read that both paths
invoke, after patching them separately failed twice in opposite directions. Two of the three shapes
you swept came back empty, which was useful. This is round 19 of a 20-round cap, so treat it as the
last substantive pass and answer in one comment: is there any remaining defect on this branch that
would cause a wrong outcome -- a merge past unread findings, a loop that does not terminate, a
verdict bound to the wrong commit or round, or an abort that loses a recovery the procedure promises?
Rank what you find by that consequence rather than by how many copies of a phrase disagree. If you
find none of that class, say so plainly and separately from any lesser wording points, because I need
to distinguish "converged" from "quiet" before this branch is merged.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=43f18a60 round=19 -->

@codex review the previous round's ordering bug is fixed: the sweep now narrows by identity alone,
drops only `DISMISSED`, and hands every surviving review to the state table, and the lower bound no
longer silently discards a draft that has no `submitted_at`. This is round 20 and the run's cap, so
whatever you return here is reported rather than merged. Same question as last round, one comment:
any remaining defect that would cause a wrong outcome -- a merge past unread findings, a loop that
does not terminate, a verdict bound to the wrong commit or round, or an abort that loses a promised
recovery -- ranked by that consequence. Include anything the last two rounds' fixes introduced, since
that has been the largest single source of defects on this branch. If there is none of that class,
say so plainly and separately from lesser points.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=b05eb1be round=20 -->

@codex review the previous run ended at its round cap with two commits nobody has reviewed: the fix
for round 20's finding, and a measurement record. Review those first. Then two questions, both in
this one comment rather than across rounds.

First, the standing one, ranked by consequence: any remaining defect that would cause a wrong outcome
-- a merge past unread findings, a loop that does not terminate, a verdict bound to the wrong commit
or round, or an abort that loses a recovery the procedure promises.

Second, a specific one I have just measured outside this branch. This file is installed as a Claude
Code slash command, and that loader substitutes positional parameters written as a dollar sign
followed by a digit before the text is read. The fenced scripts use those parameters heavily in awk
programs and in shell `set --` handling. Invoked with arguments, the loaded copy of the wait fence
had its trigger timestamp replaced by a literal and its awk field references replaced by constants,
so it selected no review at all and every round would have timed out; the CI fence turned a passing
row into a retry. Both fail closed, but the tool does not work. Tell me whether you agree that is a
real defect in this file, what the full set of affected positions is, and whether a fix is possible
that does not change the fenced bytes -- since changing them costs every user a permission
re-approval.

<!-- revloop:trigger v=1 reviewer=codex bot=chatgpt-codex-connector head=65d73ddd round=21 -->
